bioprojects.title: Mycoplasma sp. 'bovine group 7'

assembly_info.comments:
Mycoplasma leachii (formerly Mycoplasma sp. 'bovine group 7') is a recently re-named species belonging to the Mycoplasma mycoides phylogenetic cluster of ruminant mycoplasmal pathogens. The type strain PG50 was isolated in Australia in 1963 from an arthritic joint of a calf with mastitis. The culture used for this project was obtained from the Mollicutes Collection of Cultures and Antisera (http://the-iom.org/index.php?id=46), Purdue University, under the designation "PG50 [N29] bovine group 7". To minimize mutational heterogeneity in the genome sample, DNA was prepared from an axenic culture propagated from a single colony isolate (MU clone 8). The genome, consisting of a single circular chromosome, was sequenced to closure using the Sanger whole genome random shotgun method, yielding approximately 8-fold sequence coverage.

All taxa comprising the Mycoplasma mycoides cluster infect ruminant animals, in which they display a wide range of disease manifestations and severity. Specific subspecies cause two widespread and economically damaging diseases, contagious bovine pleuropneumonia (CBPP) in cattle and contagious caprine pleuropneumonia (CCPP) in goats. These and other less pathogenic subspecies of the cluster show overlaps in phenotypic traits, and incongruent phylogenetic branching based on different gene sets. Consequently taxa of this group continue to challenge the definition of species, and their selective detection and classification has required multiple approaches. Phase variable expression of surface antigens mediated by reversible indel mutation is also known to occur in two taxa of the group.

Comparison of the genome of M. leachii type str. PG50 with others in the Mycoplasma mycoides cluster reveals select regions having distinctive content or topology. Collectively, these genomic features implicate multiple evolutionary forces (including horizontal gene transfer and differential gene loss) in shaping this group of organisms, and further reveal the basis for some of their distinguishing phenotypic traits. This information may be useful in the design of disease control measures. Recently, a genome of one taxon of this cluster has been synthetically engineered and transplanted to redirect the identity of a distinct recipient taxon of the cluster, thereby ushering in the prospect of designing synthetic cells with tailored genomic content. In this regard the genome sequence of M. leachii type str. PG50 also informs the possible design of tailored synthetic genomes with specific genetic features.

This project was supported by US Department of Agriculture ARS Project 1940-32000-039-08S at the University of Missouri and the Office of Science (BER), U.S. Department of Energy, Grant No. DE-FC02-02ER63453 to the J. Craig Venter Institute.

organism.organism_name: Spiroplasma endosymbiont of Glossina fuscipes fuscipes

bioprojects.title: In vitro cultivation and genomic insights into the Spiroplasma symbiont of the tsetse fly Glossina fuscipes; implications for trypanosome transmission control

description.title: Spiroplasma glossinidia sGff culture

organism.organism_name: Spiroplasma endosymbiont of Glossina fuscipes fuscipes

description.comment: The Spiroplasma endosymbiont of Glossina fuscipes fuscipes; sGff, naturally present in some wild Glossina fuscipes fuscipes populations and 50% of the Glossina fuscipes fuscipes colony flies at the FAO/IAEA IPCL, is of biological interest due to its ability to manipulate tsetse physiology. Flies used for the initiation of the preculture were derived from a high Spiroplasma prevalence Glossina fuscipes fuscipes (Gff) laboratory line, maintained at the insectary at FAO/IAEA Insect Pest Control Laboratory (IPCL) in Seibersdorf, Austria. Fly hemolymph was extracted from 10 surface-sterilized females and 10 males aged seven to 21 days by removing one front leg and aspirating the exposed hemolymph droplet with a 10 ul pipette tip. Precultures were initiated in three biological replicates by inoculating 3.2 ml preculture media (BSK-H + 5% filtered fly extract) with 10 ul of harvested hemolymph and incubated at 25 C for 14 days without agitation under microaerobic atmospheric conditions (8-9% O2, 7-8% CO2). Precultures were pelleted by centrifugation for 40 min at 2000g, resuspended in 3.2 ml of BSK-H-spiro media (BSK-H + 7.5% fly extract, 6% rabbit serum, 0.5% Penicillin, 2.5% arginine, 5% lipid mix) and aliquots of 100 ul stored at -80 C. Cultures were prepared using 100 ul frozen preculture aliquots in 3.2 ml of BSK-H-spiro media at 25 C in microaerobic conditions without agitation for the establishment of active long-term cultures.

Manual curation and Hi-C to bring to chromosome level. HiFiasm does produce complete chromosome haplotigs for many of the chromosomes for this species, as it's a small genome. Suggest future update to would be to rerun haplotig assembly software like hifiasm or others and reannotate haplotype version. Single primary sequence assembly, not haplotype assembled. Single individual, unknown sex used for HiFi PacBio and Hi-C Illumina reads. Mixed sample with Phyllotreta striolata but one individual taken that is correct species. Taken from Canada in September 2020.

assembly_info.submitter: Research Institute for Physico-Chemical Medicine, Ministry of Public Health and Social Development of Russia
assembly_info.assembly_method: chromosome: TIGR v. 2.0; plasmids: HGAP v. 1.0
assembly_info.comments:
Annotation was added by the NCBI Prokaryotic Genome Annotation Pipeline (released 2013). Information about the Pipeline can be found here: http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genome/annotation_prok/
Bacteria available from Universite de Rennes. Source DNA available from RIPCM, Moscow.
The Spiroplasma melliferum KC3 strain was provided by Prof. H. Wroblewsky, Universite de Rennes. S. melliferum KC3 was cultured in the SP4 medium. The genome was sequenced with Sanger (the sequence coverage of both strands was 11x. For the 5x coverage of each strand error rate was 0.001) and assembled with TIGR. Moreover, two mate-paired libraries for SOLiD 4 system with inserts approximately 2.5 kb and 5.5 kb were constructed from 25g of genomic DNA for each. Fifty base reads were obtained from each of the F3 and R3 tags, with 186 million to 194 million reads obtained for each of the libraries. Then those reads were mapped to Sanger contigs with Perm software.

description.title: Deletion mutant from Mycoplasma mycoides subsp. capri strain GM12, YCpMmyc1.1-deltaglf

organism.organism_name: Mycoplasma mycoides subsp. capri str. GM12

description.comment: GM12 strain was originally isolated by Al DaMassa. In 2009 the J. Craig Venter Institute (JCVI) cloned the genome into Saccharomyces cerevisiae as a yeast centromeric plasmid and named it YCpMmyc1.1. The International Livestock Research Institute (ILRI), in collaboration with JCVI and the French National Institute for Agricultural Research (INRA), expanded on this work and then used yeast genetic tools to delete the glf gene encoding the enzyme UDP-galactopyranose mutase. The genome was transplanted from yeast into a Mycoplasma capricolum recipient cell to generate the novel mutant M. mycoides subspecies capri YCpMmyc1.1-deltaglf.

organism.organism_name: Mycoplasma mycoides subsp. capri str. GM12

assembly_info.comments:
GM12 strain was originally isolated by Al DaMassa. The J. Craig Venter Institute obtained the strain from Dr. Mary Brown at the University of Florida. In 2009 the organism was renamed.
The sequenced strain was modified by the insertion of an oriC plasmid near the genome origin of replication. The plasmid contained the following genes: tetracycline resistance marker, beta-galactosidase, ampicillin resistance marker, a second copy of the M. mycoides dnaA gene, and a fragment of the M. mycoides dnaN. Organism was recently renamed from Mycoplasma mycoides subspecies mycoides large colony type to Mycoplasma mycoides subspecies capri. The J. Craig Venter Institute (JCVI) used it as a donor genome in the first demonstration of bacterial genome transplantation

organism.organism_name: Mycoplasma mycoides subsp. capri str. GM12

assembly_info.comments:
GM12 strain was originally isolated by Al DaMassa. The J. Craig Venter Institute obtained the strain from Dr. Mary Brown at the University of Florida. In 2009 the organism was renamed.
The J. Craig Venter Institute (JCVI) used it as a donor genome in the first demonstration of bacterial genome transplantation. In 2009 the JCVI cloned the genome into Saccharomyces cerevisiae as a yeast centromeric plasmid. The JCVI then used yeast genetic tools to delete part of a type III restriction enzyme, a modification that could not be made using existing genetic tools for M. mycoides and the genome was transplanted from yeast into a Mycoplasma capricolum recipient cell to generate a novel mutant M. mycoides subspecies capri.

organism.organism_name: Mycoplasma mycoides subsp. mycoides SC str. Gladysdale

assembly_info.comments:
Mycoplasma mycoides subspecies mycoides is the etiologic agent of contagious bovine pleuropneumonia. The Gladysdale strain was isolated prior to 1964 in Australia and has been widely used as a reference strain. The source used for this project was a stock culture maintained in the Foreign Animal Disease Diagnostic Laboratory, USDA, APHIS, at the Plum Island Animal Disease Center, which was routinely used to induce and demonstrate acute pulmonary disease in cattle following tracheal inoculation. Consequently this represents an experimentally pathogenic strain. To minimize mutational heterogeneity in the genome sample, DNA was prepared from an axenic culture propagated from a single colony isolate from this stock (MU clone SC5). The genome, comprising a single circular chromosome, was sequenced to closure using the Sanger whole genome random shotgun method, yielding approximately 8-fold sequence coverage.

On a macro scale, the sequence of the Gladysdale genome generally resembles that of Mycoplasma mycoides subspecies mycoides type strain PG1 (reflecting a non-pathogenic culture), but it displays many differences ranging from single nucleotide substitutions to duplication or transpositions involving large repeats, both known and previously unknown. This genome sequence and the clonal isolate it represents provide opportunities to examine pathogenesis and population dynamics on an experimental and genomic level.

This project was supported by US Department of Agriculture ARS Project 1940-32000-039-08S at the University of Missouri and the Office of Science (BER), U.S. Department of Energy, Grant No. DE-FC02-02ER63453 to the J. Craig Venter Institute.

description.title: Spiroplasma citri LB 319
description.comment: Using LD8 medium, S. citri strain BR12 was isolated from brittle root near Collinsville, IL on 7/24/84 and maintained in culture. For sequencing, S. citri strain BR12 was triple-cloned and cultured in LD8 medium to obtain enough DNA for sequencing. Total genomic DNA was extracted using CTAB method and library was prepared for sequencing using PacBio SMRTbell Express Template Prep Kit. Whole-genome sequencing was performed on the PacBio RS II platform. Reads were filtered and assembled using SMRT Analysis software from PacBio with default settings.

bioprojects.title: Mycoplasma capricolum subsp. capricolum strain:GM508D Genome sequencing and assembly

description.title: Microbe sample from Mycoplasma capricolum subsp. capricolum
description.comment: Received in June 1985 from Al DaMassa (Univ. Calif. Davis). Isolated from a septicemia in a late-term, aborted, caprine fetus (Toggenburg). Glucose and arginine positive strain. Weak growth inhibition to Calif. kid type strain. Culture not cloned.

attributes.name: isolation_source
attributes.value: septicemia in a late-term, aborted, caprine fetus

biosample.isolation_source: septicemia in a late-term, aborted, caprine fetus

assembly_info.comments:
There is a duplicated sequence that (by the simplest model) would be approx. 34 kb. This has prevented closure of the genome. The termini of the submitted sequence are likely to be separated by 14 kb (that would be a duplicated sequence of that between MCP508_00065 and MCP508_00120). Apart from 1 SNP that we have detected, we expect the entire duplicated region to be
100% identical and therefore cannot be sequenced by next generation technologies (not even PacBio long reads, with which this was generated).

PacBio was able to assemble the region that corresponds to the first 5 ORFs, despite this being "identical" to MCP508_00120 to MCP508_00135. Similarly at the 3' end of the submission, the last 5 ORFs are duplications of MCP508_ 00045 through MCP508_00065. The junction of the duplicated region is the hybrid/fused gene clpB-lppD gene (/locus_tag="MCP508_00040"). Full length copies of each of these genes are present (MCP508_00150 and MCP508_04400). The junction of the duplicated region has been independently verified also.

description.comment: Using LD8 medium, S. citri strain BLH-MB was isolated from beet leafhopper collected from Russian thisle in 2011 near Parlier, CA and maintained in culture. For sequencing, S. citri strain BLH-MB was triple-cloned and cultured in LD8 medium to obtain enough DNA for sequencing. Total genomic DNA was extracted using CTAB method and library was prepared for sequencing using PacBio SMRTbell Express Template Prep Kit. Whole-genome sequencing was performed on the PacBio RS II platform. Reads were filtered and assembled using SMRT Analysis software from PacBio with default settings.
